angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 726,311 km at 79.43 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.5896 +/- 0.0122 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 79.43 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.044 +/- 0.024 solar radii from Nies et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 21520 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.534.3744N/abstract): 726,311 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.09 +/- 0.07 solar masses from Nies et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 21520 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.534.3744N/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5871 +/- 62 K from Nies et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 21520 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.534.3744N/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Nies et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 21520 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.534.3744N/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-21520.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.438, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
